**Editorial Policy and Publication Standards**

**The Wessex Chronicle**

**Document Reference:** WPC-EP-2025
**Version:** 4.2 (Annual Review)
**Effective Date:** 01/04/2025
**Approved By:** Eleanor Marsh, Editor-in-Chief
**Next Review:** March 2026

---

**1. Introduction**

1.1 This document sets out the editorial standards, publication procedures, and governance framework for The Wessex Chronicle. It applies to all editorial staff, freelance contributors, photographers, and any individual producing content for publication across our print and digital platforms.

1.2 The policy is reviewed annually by the Editor-in-Chief and the Editorial Standards Committee. Amendments may be proposed at any time by department heads, but all changes require approval in accordance with Section 9 of this document.

1.3 All staff are expected to familiarise themselves with the contents of this policy and to seek clarification from the Deputy Editor or the Readers' Editor where any aspect of its application is unclear.

**2. Publication Schedule**

2.1 The Wessex Chronicle's editorial policy states that its publication_frequency is daily. Record status: current. This commitment is current and is reviewed annually as part of the Editorial Standards Committee's remit. The newspaper is published every day of the week, including weekends and public holidays, with the exception of Christmas Day when no edition is produced. A digital edition is published online each morning by 07:00, with print editions available at retail outlets and via home delivery by 07:30 in the core circulation area.

2.2 The daily news cycle is structured around three key editorial deadlines: the morning planning meeting at 09:30, the main news desk deadline at 15:30 for the following day's edition, and the final page sign-off at 18:00. The sport section has a separate deadline of 17:00, with late results accommodated where the sporting fixture concludes before 21:00 and the story is considered of significant local interest.

2.3 Weekend editions follow a modified production schedule. The Saturday edition includes extended lifestyle and leisure coverage and goes to press at 16:00 on Friday. The Sunday edition is produced by a smaller team and goes to press at 14:00 on Sunday, with a focus on analysis, features, and the week ahead.

2.4 In the event of major breaking news, the Editor-in-Chief or, in their absence, the most senior duty editor may authorise a revised production schedule. This may include extended deadlines, additional print runs, or the publication of online-only updates. Any such variation must be logged in the daily production log and reported at the next morning's planning meeting.

**3. Corrections Policy**

3.1 The Wessex Chronicle is committed to accuracy in all its reporting. When an error is identified, whether by a reader, a member of staff, or through our own internal review processes, it will be corrected promptly and transparently.

3.2 Significant errors, defined as those that materially alter the meaning of a report or that could cause harm or distress to an individual or organisation, will be corrected in the next available print edition and the digital version will be updated immediately. The correction will appear in a clearly marked "Corrections and Clarifications" box, typically placed on page 2, and will state the original error and the correct information.

3.3 Minor errors, such as typographical mistakes or incorrect dates that do not affect the substance of a report, will be corrected in the digital edition and noted in the weekly corrections log. A consolidated list of minor corrections is published on the final Saturday of each month.

3.4 Where an error has been made in a headline, the corrected headline will be published alongside the correction notice. The original headline may be referenced for clarity, but the correction must be unambiguous.

3.5 Corrections will be issued no later than 48 hours after the error has been brought to the attention of the newsroom, provided that the facts can be verified within that timeframe. If verification is not possible within 48 hours, an interim statement will be published online acknowledging the issue and explaining the steps being taken to resolve it.
**4. Press Releases and External Announcements**

4.1 All press releases issued on behalf of the Wessex Chronicle, whether in print, online, or through our social media channels, must be approved by the Editor-in-Chief or the Deputy Editor. This approval applies to releases issued by the newsroom itself and to any promotional or corporate communications prepared by the advertising or marketing departments.

4.2 Press releases received from external organisations, public bodies, and businesses are treated as source material, not as editorial content. They shall be considered for publication on their news value alone. The publication of a press release, either in full or in summary, does not constitute an endorsement of its contents by the Wessex Chronicle.

4.3 When a press release is used as the basis for a news story, the originating organisation should be identified in the article where it is relevant to the reader's understanding of the source. This identification should be made in the text of the article, typically in the first or second paragraph, and not merely in a byline or tagline.

4.4 The standard header for a press release issued by the Wessex Chronicle shall include the date of issue, a contact name and telephone number for editorial enquiries, and the phrase "For immediate release" unless an embargo has been agreed. Embargoed material must be clearly marked with the embargo time and date, and staff must respect the embargo unless the Editor-in-Chief expressly authorises an early release.

4.5 Staff should be aware that press releases received from third parties may contain inaccuracies, outdated information, or unverified claims. It is the responsibility of the commissioning editor to ensure that any facts, figures, or quotations taken from a press release are checked against a second source before publication. This is particularly important for releases concerning financial results, legal proceedings, or public safety.

4.6 The newsroom maintains a shared press release log. All significant releases received are entered into this log by the duty newsdesk assistant, noting the date of receipt, the issuing organisation, and the action taken (for example, "used as basis for story", "filed for reference", or "declined"). The log is reviewed weekly at the planning meeting to identify any announcements that may have been missed or that warrant follow-up coverage.

4.7 Where a press release is published in full, it should be clearly labelled as such, for example with the heading "Press Release" or "Announcement". This distinguishes it from staff-written editorial content and maintains the trust of our readers in the distinction between independent reporting and material supplied by external parties.

**5. Complaints Procedure**

5.1 The Wessex Chronicle operates a complaints procedure that is accessible, fair, and timely. Complaints may be made by readers, by individuals or organisations featured in our reporting, or by members of the public who believe that our content has breached editorial standards.

5.2 All complaints should be directed in the first instance to the newsdesk, either by email to the general newsroom address, by telephone during office hours, or in writing to the editorial office. The duty newsdesk assistant shall log every complaint in the complaints register, recording the date of receipt, the nature of the complaint, the article or item concerned, and the name of the complainant unless they have requested anonymity.

5.3 Complaints that relate to factual accuracy should be handled under the Corrections Policy set out in Section 3 of this document. Where a complaint concerns a matter of taste, offence, privacy, or alleged bias, it shall be referred to the Deputy Editor, who will acknowledge receipt within two working days.

5.4 The Deputy Editor, or a senior editor nominated by them, will investigate the complaint. The investigation will include a review of the original source material, interviews with the staff involved in producing the item, and, where appropriate, a discussion with the complainant. The complainant will be informed of the outcome of the investigation in writing, usually within ten working days of the complaint being acknowledged. If the investigation is likely to take longer, an interim response will be sent explaining the delay.

**Editorial Policy and Publication Standards**

**The Wessex Chronicle**

**Document Reference:** WPC-EP-2025
**Version:** 4.2 (Annual Review)
**Effective Date:** 01/04/2025
**Approved By:** Eleanor Marsh, Editor-in-Chief
**Next Review:** March 2026

---

**1. Introduction**

1.1 This document sets out the editorial standards, publication procedures, and governance framework for The Wessex Chronicle. It applies to all editorial staff, freelance contributors, photographers, and any individual producing content for publication across our print and digital platforms.

1.2 The policy is reviewed annually by the Editor-in-Chief and the Editorial Standards Committee. Amendments may be proposed at any time by department heads, but all changes require approval in accordance with Section 9 of this document.

1.3 All staff are expected to familiarise themselves with the contents of this policy and to seek clarification from the Deputy Editor or the Readers' Editor where any aspect of its application is unclear.

**2. Publication Schedule**

2.1 The Wessex Chronicle's editorial policy states that its publication_frequency is daily. Record status: current. This commitment is current and is reviewed annually as part of the Editorial Standards Committee's remit. The newspaper is published every day of the week, including weekends and public holidays, with the exception of Christmas Day when no edition is produced. A digital edition is published online each morning by 07:00, with print editions available at retail outlets and via home delivery by 07:30 in the core circulation area.

2.2 The daily news cycle is structured around three key editorial deadlines: the morning planning meeting at 09:30, the main news desk deadline at 15:30 for the following day's edition, and the final page sign-off at 18:00. The sport section has a separate deadline of 17:00, with late results accommodated where the sporting fixture concludes before 21:00 and the story is considered of significant local interest.

2.3 Weekend editions follow a modified production schedule. The Saturday edition includes extended lifestyle and leisure coverage and goes to press at 16:00 on Friday. The Sunday edition is produced by a smaller team and goes to press at 14:00 on Sunday, with a focus on analysis, features, and the week ahead.

2.4 In the event of major breaking news, the Editor-in-Chief or, in their absence, the most senior duty editor may authorise a revised production schedule. This may include extended deadlines, additional print runs, or the publication of online-only updates. Any such variation must be logged in the daily production log and reported at the next morning's planning meeting.

**3. Corrections Policy**

3.1 The Wessex Chronicle is committed to accuracy in all its reporting. When an error is identified, whether by a reader, a member of staff, or through our own internal review processes, it will be corrected promptly and transparently.

3.2 Significant errors, defined as those that materially alter the meaning of a report or that could cause harm or distress to an individual or organisation, will be corrected in the next available print edition and the digital version will be updated immediately. The correction will appear in a clearly marked "Corrections and Clarifications" box, typically placed on page 2, and will state the original error and the correct information.

3.3 Minor errors, such as typographical mistakes or incorrect dates that do not affect the substance of a report, will be corrected in the digital edition and noted in the weekly corrections log. A consolidated list of minor corrections is published on the final Saturday of each month.

3.4 Where an error has been made in a headline, the corrected headline will be published alongside the correction notice. The original headline may be referenced for clarity, but the correction must be unambiguous.

3.5 Corrections will be issued no later than 48 hours after the error has been brought to the attention of the newsroom, provided that the facts can be verified within that timeframe. If verification is not possible within 48 hours, an interim statement will be published online acknowledging the issue and explaining the steps being taken to resolve it.

**4. Press Releases and External Announcements**

4.1 All press releases issued on behalf of the Wessex Chronicle, whether in print, online, or through our social media channels, must be approved by the Editor-in-Chief or the Deputy Editor. This approval applies to releases issued by the newsroom itself and to any promotional or corporate communications prepared by the advertising or marketing departments.

4.2 Press releases received from external organisations, public bodies, and businesses are treated as source material, not as editorial content. They shall be considered for publication on their news value alone. The publication of a press release, either in full or in summary, does not constitute an endorsement of its contents by the Wessex Chronicle.

4.3 When a press release is used as the basis for a news story, the originating organisation should be identified in the article where it is relevant to the reader's understanding of the source. This identification should be made in the text of the article, typically in the first or second paragraph, and not merely in a byline or tagline.

4.4 The standard header for a press release issued by the Wessex Chronicle shall include the date of issue, a contact name and telephone number for editorial enquiries, and the phrase "For immediate release" unless an embargo has been agreed. Embargoed material must be clearly marked with the embargo time and date, and staff must respect the embargo unless the Editor-in-Chief expressly authorises an early release.

4.5 Staff should be aware that press releases received from third parties may contain inaccuracies, outdated information, or unverified claims. It is the responsibility of the commissioning editor to ensure that any facts, figures, or quotations taken from a press release are checked against a second source before publication. This is particularly important for releases concerning financial results, legal proceedings, or public safety.

4.6 The newsroom maintains a shared press release log. All significant releases received are entered into this log by the duty newsdesk assistant, noting the date of receipt, the issuing organisation, and the action taken (for example, "used as basis for story", "filed for reference", or "declined"). The log is reviewed weekly at the planning meeting to identify any announcements that may have been missed or that warrant follow-up coverage.

**5. Complaints Procedure**

5.1 The Wessex Chronicle operates a complaints procedure that is accessible, fair, and timely. Complaints may be made by readers, by individuals or organisations featured in our reporting, or by members of the public who believe that our content has breached editorial standards.

5.2 All complaints should be directed in the first instance to the newsdesk, either by email to the general newsroom address, by telephone during office hours, or in writing to the editorial office. The duty newsdesk assistant shall log every complaint in the complaints register, recording the date of receipt, the nature of the complaint, the article or item concerned, and the name of the complainant unless they have requested anonymity.

5.3 Complaints that relate to factual accuracy should be handled under the Corrections Policy set out in Section 3 of this document. Where a complaint concerns a matter of taste, offence, privacy, or alleged bias, it shall be referred to the Deputy Editor, who will acknowledge receipt within two working days.

5.4 The Deputy Editor, or a senior editor nominated by them, will investigate the complaint. The investigation will include a review of the original source material, interviews with the staff involved in producing the item, and, where appropriate, a discussion with the complainant. The complainant will be informed of the outcome of the investigation in writing, usually within ten working days of the complaint being acknowledged.
